target.title: fix(openshell): bound sandbox readFile with size cap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `readFile` method in `extensions/openshell/src/fs-bridge.ts` (line 72) opens a file through the sandbox bridge and calls `handle.readFile()` to read the entire file as a Buffer with no size limit. A sandboxed process could request reading a multi-GB file, causing OOM in the host process.

While the sandbox already validates path safety (symlinks, hardlinks), it imposes no size limit on file reads.

## Why This Change Was Made

Unbounded file reads in the sandbox bridge is a real OOM vector. A sandboxed agent process can request arbitrary file reads through the `SandboxFsBridge` interface, and without a size cap, a large file (or a compromised sandbox process) could exhaust host memory.

## What Changed

Added a `handle.stat()` check before `readFile()` in `OpenShellFsBridge.readFile`:
1. Stats the opened file handle
2. Rejects non-regular files
3. Rejects files exceeding 100 MiB cap
4. Only proceeds to `readFile()` for files that pass the checks

## User Impact

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| Sandbox read of 10 GB file → host OOM | → rejected with "file too large" |
| Normal sandbox file reads → works | → works (unchanged) |

## Evidence

**All 56 openshell tests pass:**

```
✓ extensions/openshell (4 test files, 56 passed)
```

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Running sessions in the sidebar show no hint of what the agent is actually doing — you open each one to find out. The model constantly narrates its work ("Rebasing onto main and rerunning the sidebar suite."), but that stream never reaches the sidebar.

## Why This Change Was Made

Maintainer-requested (part of the sidebar program with #111035): while a session runs, its row shows a live activity subtitle derived from the model's newest narration, web-side only (no gateway changes), behind a synced preference defaulting to on.

## User Impact

- Rows with an active run show the model's latest sentence as a subtitle (markdown stripped, ≤120 chars, subtle crossfade, updates throttled to 2s); when the newest signal is a tool call, the subtitle falls back to the real tool name ("Using exec"). Resting rows stay title-only; run end removes the line.
- Priority: automatic attention (question/approval/error from #111035) always outranks narration; narration outranks the worktree subtitle. Catalog display-object subtitle semantics preserved.
- Purely client-side: the sidebar opens `sessions.messages.subscribe` for up to 6 running rows (newest first; the open chat session's subscription is never touched since the per-connection subscription set is shared, not refcounted), unsubscribes on run end/row removal/disconnect, and resubscribes after reconnect.
- Privacy hardening (driven by nine autoreview rounds): internal-runtime context blocks are suppressed fragment-aware including truncated/nested/partial-delimiter cases; heartbeat/control-reply tokens never render; a mid-run join stays silent until a cumulative snapshot aligns the stream (a bare first delta could be the inside of an internal block); empty or suppressed-only replacements retract the shown line, including anything still queued behind the throttle.
- Performance: append detection is length arithmetic on the cumulative stream (O(delta) per event, resets are O(snapshot) and rare) — long background responses can't go quadratic across six subscriptions.
- Preference "Show live agent activity in sidebar" (default on, only the off-override persists) in Settings, synced via ui.prefs; off = no subscriptions, no rendering.

target.title: fix(browser): prove post-action target continuity before adopting a tab
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a browser navigation or action invalidates the selected raw target, route code retried tab lists and adopted replacements via heuristics: any sole remaining tab, a uniquely new post-action tab, or a uniquely URL-matching tab. None of those prove the acted-on page identity, so `/act` could return an unrelated tab's `targetId` and silently redirect the caller's next mutating action onto the wrong page.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper's recommended path for the route-safety fix: make each backend return its operation-owned target outcome; remove route-level list inference entirely. Playwright navigate/act now read the acted-on page's raw target id via `Target.getTargetInfo` after the operation and return it on the result. Routes apply `resolveOperationTargetOutcome`: backend-reported id when present, otherwise the acted-on id (stale/closed) so callers require a fresh selection.

Removed heuristics:
- adopting a uniquely new post-action tab
- adopting a uniquely URL-matching tab (renderer swap inferred from lists)
- sole remaining tab fallback

Extension-relay profiles use the same Playwright `readPageTargetId` backend for navigate/act outcomes (no route-level list inference). Chrome MCP existing-session uses tab-list membership via `readChromeMcpOperationTargetId` after navigate/act; close reports `operationTargetId: null`.

**Deferred (separate browser-contract PR):** extension-relay opaque public CDP target handles (`openclaw-relay-<nonce>-<ordinal>`) and relay-bridge identity migration. This PR intentionally does not change `relay-bridge.ts` public target IDs so route safety can land without a compatibility-sensitive relay contract decision.

## User Impact

- **Playwright navigate/act:** response `targetId` is the backend-owned identity of the page that executed the operation. If the page closes, the acted-on id is returned (stale) and callers must re-select.
- **Extension-relay /navigate and /act:** route applies `resolveOperationTargetOutcome` to `readPageTargetId` outcomes (no list inference). Relay CDP public target IDs are unchanged from current main.
- **Chrome MCP existing-session /act:** route applies `resolveOperationTargetOutcome` to tab-list membership; stale acted-on id preserved when the tab is gone.
- **No wrong-tab routing:** unrelated tabs left open are never adopted from tab lists, URL cardinality, or sole-tab fallback.
- **Continuity preserved:** renderer swaps and action-triggered replacements still work when the backend reports the new raw target id (#25323 / #25326 / #46137).

## Evidence

### Live browser proof (real Chrome/CDP, route-level contracts)

Harness: `extensions/browser/scripts/proof-103785-target-continuity.test-harness.mts`

Run:

```
pnpm exec tsx extensions/browser/scripts/proof-103785-target-continuity.test-harness.mts
```

Redacted output:

```
=== Live-browser proof for #103785 (backend-owned page identity) ===

Scenario A: action closes acted-on tab A; unrelated tab B survives
  kept acted-on identity A: true
  adopted unrelated survivor B: false
  PASS: unrelated survivor B was NOT adopted.

Scenario B: renderer swap (page reattaches under new raw target at navigated url)
  adopted backend-reported reattached target: true
  PASS: renderer-swap continuity preserved.

Scenario C: extension-relay /navigate route (readPageTargetId post-navigate + route resolver)
  readPageTargetId (navigateViaPlaywright return contract)=A37CCE32… url=http://[redacted-host]/…
  /navigate route outcome target=A37CCE32… (acted-on=A37CCE32…)
  adopted backend-reported post-navigate target: true
  PASS: extension-relay route preserved backend-owned identity.

Scenario D: Chrome MCP existing-session /act route (tab-list membership + resolver)
  D1 tab still in list: kept acted-on identity when tab survives: true
  D2 tab gone after close: stale acted-on id preserved when tab is gone: true
  PASS: Chrome MCP route contract honored for survive + close.

=== ALL SCENARIOS PASSED ===
```

Scenario C exercises the extension-relay route resolver over real Chrome via Playwright `readPageTargetId` (the same backend path extension-relay profiles use). It does not change relay-bridge public CDP target IDs.

### Deferred relay public-ID migration

Follow-up work (not in this PR): instance-scoped opaque relay handles, bridge regressions, and live paired Chrome extension proof for detach/reattach continuity. Requires `@steipete` browser-contract approval before landing.

### Source and test changes

- `resolveOperationTargetOutcome` replaces list-inference resolver; no tab-list adoption.
- `readPageTargetId` exported from Playwright session; `navigateViaPlaywright` and `executeActViaPlaywright` return `targetId`.
- `readChromeMcpOperationTargetId` exported; Chrome MCP existing-session `/act` and close wire operation-owned outcomes.
- Extension-relay `/navigate` and Playwright `/act` paths wire backend outcomes via `resolveOperationTargetOutcome`.
- `relay-bridge.ts` unchanged from main (relay public-ID migration deferred).

Automated tests:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.snapshot.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/server.agent-contract-core.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-relay/relay-bridge.test.ts
# 45 passed
```

Extension package boundary typecheck: `extension package boundary check passed`.

Closes #103785

target.title: fix(agent): recover disconnected gateway runs before rerunning
target.body:
Closes #98200

Supersedes #97903 and builds on the fresh-session containment landed in #110226.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw agent` could execute a turn twice after an uncertain CLI-to-Gateway disconnect: the detached Gateway run could continue while the CLI automatically started a fresh embedded fallback, duplicating model cost, mutating tool effects, and possibly `--deliver` output.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI now reconnects and calls `agent.wait` for the original run, then performs a cache-only idempotent replay to retrieve its exact terminal response. The Gateway rejects a replay-only cache miss without admitting new work. If the original outcome still cannot be proven, the CLI fails closed by default; `--rerun-on-ambiguous` is the explicit opt-in escape hatch and still uses an isolated `gateway-fallback-*` session.

This keeps result recovery at the Gateway run owner boundary and avoids transcript-tail heuristics. It also covers disconnects where the CLI never observed the `accepted` frame, because recovery uses the original idempotency key generated before dispatch.

## User Impact

Users no longer get an automatic duplicate execution after an ambiguous Gateway close or timeout. Successful recovery prints the original result, known terminal failures remain failures, and unknown outcomes stop safely with the run id and a warning that no fallback started. Users who knowingly accept duplicate-side-effect risk can opt into a fresh embedded rerun with `--rerun-on-ambiguous`.

This is a compatibility-sensitive change from the automatic fresh-session fallback currently on `main`. The default ambiguity policy remains subject to the maintainer decision requested in #98200.

## Evidence

- Real Gateway recovery proof: [GitHub Actions run 29672759141](https://github.com/youngting520/openclaw/actions/runs/29672759141) passed on PR source `60083df0567` using a proof-only fork workflow wrapper.
  - Setup: real `openclaw agent` CLI, real Gateway child, WebSocket fault proxy, deterministic mock model provider.
  - Controlled fault: terminate the CLI connection after the Gateway returns `accepted` while the original run remains active.
  - Captured recovery RPCs: `agent -> agent.wait -> agent(replayOnly=true)`.
  - Recovered CLI output: `GATEWAY-RECOVERY-OK`.
  - Provider request count: `1`, proving recovery did not start a second model turn.
  - Replay-only cache miss: `AGENT_RESULT_NOT_FOUND`; provider request delta remained `0`.
  - Vitest result: 1 file passed, 1 test passed, 53.55s total.
- The live proof is committed as `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/agent-gateway-recovery.e2e.test.ts`.
- Focused Vitest run on Node 22.22.3: 4 shards passed, 119 tests passed, 1 existing test skipped.
  - `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/error-codes.test.ts`
  - `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/agent.test.ts`
  - `src/gateway/server-methods/agent-request-preflight.replay-only.test.ts`
  - `src/cli/program/register.agent.test.ts`
  - `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts`
- `replayOnly` reads the existing process-local Gateway dedupe map. It does not add or change a persistent cache or stored-data schema, so no migration is required.
- `oxfmt --check` passed for the original 11 touched files; `git diff --check` also passes for the added E2E.
- Full PR CI remains gated while the PR is a draft pending the ambiguity-policy decision in #98200.
- Mandatory autoreview was retried for each E2E edit using the trusted `main` helper. The bundle passed its secret scan, but the Codex engine process exited without a structured verdict on every attempt; no alternative model was substituted.

target.title: fix(plugins): surface oversized-file warnings in doctor migration reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three plugin doctor-contract files read legacy state files during `openclaw doctor` migration with a TOCTOU-prone pattern: `statSync(path)` checks file size (10 MiB cap), then a separate `await fs.readFile(path)` reads the content. Between the stat and the read, a file could be swapped with a much larger one, bypassing the size cap and potentially causing OOM.

Affected files:

1. **Reef** (`extensions/reef/doctor-contract-api.ts`): Two read sites for identity keys and binding registrations
2. **Active Memory** (`extensions/active-memory/doctor-contract-api.ts`): Reads legacy session-toggle JSON
3. **Device Pair** (`extensions/device-pair/doctor-contract-api.ts`): Reads legacy notify state JSON

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor migration runs during `openclaw doctor`, triggered by users to diagnose their installation. While the 10 MiB cap is reasonable, the stat-then-read pattern has a TOCTOU race: the stat validates one file's size, but the read may consume a different (potentially unbounded) file. Opening the file first and operating on the same descriptor eliminates this race.

## What Changed

All three `readLegacy*FileSafely` helpers now use descriptor-bound reads:

```typescript
const file = await fs.open(filePath, "r");
try {
  const stat = await file.stat();
  if (!stat.isFile()) throw new Error("not a regular file");
  if (stat.size > MAX_BYTES) throw new Error("file too large");
  return await file.readFile("utf8");
} finally {
  await file.close();
}
```

- `fs.promises.open()` returns a `FileHandle` — `stat()` and `readFile()` both operate on the same descriptor
- `try/finally` guarantees `file.close()` even when exceptions are thrown
- Removed unused `import { statSync }` from all three files
- Warning-aware error path for oversized files preserved exactly

## User Impact

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| `statSync(path)` → TOCTOU race: file could be swapped before read | → fd pins the inode; race impossible |
| Doctor migration with valid legacy state → works | → works (unchanged) |
| Corrupted oversized file → caught with warning | → caught (unchanged, but without TOCTOU) |

## Evidence

**Extension tests pass (active-memory + reef = 462 total):**

```
 ✓ extensions/active-memory (4 test files, 201 passed)
 ✓ extensions/reef (24 test files, 261 passed, 2 skipped)
```

(Device Pair tests excluded due to pre-existing dependency on an unmerged migration PR.)

The descriptor-bound pattern is the standard fix for TOCTOU file races — the fd pins the specific inode, preventing substitution between validation and consumption.

target.title: fix(fleet): gateway token is echoed raw to the terminal in create and restore commands
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the `openclaw fleet create` and `openclaw fleet restore` commands echo the full 32-character hex gateway authentication token to the terminal in human-readable output. This token authenticates the fleet container to the gateway and is treated as sensitive elsewhere in the codebase — the fleet service explicitly redacts it from container log output. Terminal output is captured in shell history files, terminal scrollback buffers, CI/CD logs, and shell redirects, so raw tokens persist long after the command completes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two human-readable output lines now pass the token through `maskApiKey()` — the same credential-masking function used by `openclaw models status` and `openclaw models auth list` — which shows only a short prefix/suffix hint (e.g. `s...t`) instead of the full 32-character value. The `--json` output path is intentionally unchanged: structured output is consumed by automation tools that need the real token value, and callers who pass `--json` are expected to handle the credential securely.

## User Impact

`openclaw fleet create` and `openclaw fleet restore` now display a masked token in human-readable terminal output instead of the full raw value. Automation scripts that use `--json` output continue receiving the real token and are unaffected.

## Evidence

### Runtime output (before vs after)

Before: `fleet create` echoes the raw hex token to the terminal:
```
Token: 3a7f09b2c41d8e65f01a2b4c9d6e807f
```

After: the token is masked, showing only its structure while hiding the actual credential:
```
Token: 3a...7f
```

target.title: fix(plugins): load newest managed generation when a prior install lingers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #107228. After upgrading a long-lived install, a plugin's newly-installed
version can silently fail to take effect: `openclaw plugins inspect <id>
--runtime` reports the old version and `install`/`update`/sync appear to no-op.

Root cause: a managed install/update writes the new version into a distinct
managed project directory (an `__openclaw-generation__` dir) **without removing**
the prior flat project dir. The persisted install-index record keeps pointing at
the older, still-present directory. At load time `mergeRecoveredManagedNpmRecord`
(`src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-record-reader.ts`) reconciles the persisted
record against a fresh disk scan, but its self-heal branches only cover (a) the
persisted path being **gone** (`isUnavailableManagedNpmInstallRecord`), and (b) a
newer version at the **same** path. The upgrade case — persisted path still
present, the same plugin id discovered at a **different**, newer generation dir —
falls through to `return params.persisted`, so the runtime imports the stale
directory.

## Fix

1. **Recover the newest install, not an arbitrary one.**
   `buildRecoveredManagedNpmInstallRecords` previously let whichever project root
   sorted last win for a given plugin id. Generation-dir suffixes are content
   hashes, so on-disk order is unrelated to version. It now folds records through
   `pickNewerRecoveredManagedNpmRecord`, keeping the highest semver across the
   legacy flat dir and every generation dir (ties still prefer the later
   candidate, preserving generation-over-flat behavior).
2. **Repoint to the newer managed install.** When the recovered managed install
   is a strictly newer version at a different path, adopt it — reusing the same
   `mergeRecoveredManagedNpmMetadata(..., { preservePersistedSpec: true })` the
   path-gone branch uses. Gated on `isManagedNpmInstallPath`, so it only applies
   to persisted records inside the managed npm root; intentional custom/outside
   npm installs are left untouched.

Because this is a recovery-layer self-heal, it also repairs installs that have
**already** diverged from an earlier upgrade, not just future ones.

## Evidence

Focused tests in `src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-generation-precedence.test.ts`:

- **repoints to a newer managed generation when the persisted install still
  exists** — the upgrade case with the old dir present on disk (not covered by
  `isUnavailableManagedNpmInstallRecord`); asserts `installPath` / `version` /
  `spec` / `resolvedSpec`.
- **adopts the highest version when several generations are present** — pins
  version-based (not sort-order) selection.
- **keeps a current managed install when only an older generation lingers** —
  guard against an older generation superseding a current install.
- **does not repoint an intentional custom npm install outside the managed
  root** — guard for the managed-path gate.

Local run (this checkout's `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` wrapper is missing a dep, so
invoked vitest directly):

```
$ node_modules/.bin/vitest run \
    src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-generation-precedence.test.ts \
    src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-records.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  34 passed (34)
```

Confirmed the primary "repoints…" and "custom npm install outside the managed
root" tests **fail on unpatched code** (revert the source change → those tests go
red) and **pass with the fix**. Existing recovery/index suites
(`installed-plugin-index.test.ts`, `installed-plugin-index-records.test.ts`, …)
remain green.

**Real-world verification (redacted; full before/after terminal output in a PR
comment):** on a live install upgraded 2026.6.11 → 2026.7.1 where two bundled
providers' flat (2026.6.11) and `__openclaw-generation__` (2026.7.1) dirs coexist,
the **unpatched** runtime (`openclaw plugins inspect … --runtime`) loads
**2026.6.11 from the flat dir**; running the **patched** recovery against
byte-for-byte copies of those real directories resolves **2026.7.1 from the
generation dir** for both providers, while a custom install outside the managed
npm root is left unchanged.

## Scope / caveats

- **Downgrades are intentionally not auto-adopted.** If a persisted record is
  newer than a lingering directory, the persisted record is kept rather than
  silently downgrading; an explicit downgrade should update the persisted record
  at the install layer.
- This resolves the **load-time symptom** at the recovery layer. If the
  install/update flow should also repoint the persisted record when it writes a
  new generation dir, that is a complementary fix in the install pipeline.

target.title: feat(talk): durable client voice sessions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Voice conversations in Talk are ephemeral today. A client-owned realtime call (iOS WebRTC, the Control UI, or a gateway-relay fallback) speaks directly to the provider; if the transport drops, everything said is lost, nothing lands in the agent's chat history, and any tool action the voice model triggers leaves no trail. This makes voice a second-class surface: you can't scroll back through a call, other clients never see it, and there's no record of what a voice request changed.

This change makes a voice call **part of your normal agent session** across every client that can run Talk, and adds a safety gate for high-impact actions requested by voice.

## Why This Change Was Made

The design deliberately reuses existing session machinery instead of a parallel store:

- **Voice utterances live-append into the canonical agent session transcript.** A Talk consult is already a plain `chat.send` on the agent's main session, so finalized user/assistant utterances are appended as ordinary transcript messages (idempotent by a `voice:<voiceSessionId>:<entryId>` event id). They show up in web chat and every other connected client, and later consults see them as normal history — no transcript-threading or import step.
  - Client-owned transports (iOS WebRTC, Control UI) report finalized utterances via the new `talk.client.transcript` RPC.
  - Gateway-relay sessions record server-side at the existing final-transcript seam, so **Android and every relay fallback get durable voice history with no client changes**.
- **A small per-agent SQLite call record** (in the agent cache DB — no schema bump) tracks the logical call across transport restarts, the consult runs it spawned, and which mutating tools ran. It powers reconnect continuity, abandoned-call recovery, and the post-call summary.
- **Run-scoped spoken confirmation** pauses high-impact tools (message send, node/gateway/browser/computer control, cron, destructive shell, publication) invoked by a voice-originated run until the user gives an exact spoken "yes". Approval binds to a sha256 fingerprint of the tool+args and is consumed once, so the model can't confirm one action and run another. Concurrent non-voice runs on the same session are unaffected. Capability is negotiated explicitly (clients declare `voice-transcript`), so deployed clients that predate this protocol keep prior behavior rather than getting stuck at an unconfirmable pause.
- **Provider profile context** (the existing bounded IDENTITY/USER/SOUL bundle that Discord voice already injects) is added to the realtime provider session, scoped to the bound agent.
- **A mutation-only "Voice call changes" digest** is delivered to the session's last non-WebChat channel when a call that changed something ends.

**Zero new configuration** — everything is always on. No `openclaw.json` fields, env vars, or CLI flags were added.

This supersedes the durable-voice-session direction from #109376 (thanks @clifton, credited as co-author); the reshaped architecture live-appends into the session rather than maintaining a parallel ledger, keys confirmation by the consult run rather than the shared session, negotiates transcript capability explicitly, and drops the `--legacy-direct-auth` credential-in-QR workaround.

## User Impact

- Voice calls appear in your agent session history on every client, live, and survive transport drops (reconnect resumes the same logical call).
- Abandoned calls (app killed mid-call) are recovered and their transcript imported on your next call.
- High-impact actions asked for by voice require an explicit spoken confirmation before they run.
- After a call that changed something, you get a short "Voice call changes" summary on your usual channel.
- No configuration or migration for operators; existing config is untouched. Cross-client (iOS/web/relay/Android); macOS has no realtime voice today and is unchanged.
- Two new additive gateway RPCs (`talk.client.transcript`, `talk.client.close`) and optional `voiceSessionId`/`capabilities` fields on existing Talk methods; generated Swift/Kotlin/TS clients are regenerated. Server-owned relay/managed-room responses keep `voiceSessionId` optional so older gateways/clients interoperate.

## Evidence

- New/changed Vitest coverage across the confirmation gate, SQLite call record, transcript append/dedup, relay persistence, protocol scopes, and the Control UI transcript queue: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/talk/client-voice-session.test.ts src/talk/client-voice-confirmation.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/talk.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/talk-client.test.ts src/gateway/talk-realtime-relay.test.ts src/talk/agent-consult-tool.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/realtime-talk.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/realtime-talk-consult.test.ts` — all pass (178 focused tests).
- Protocol generators regenerated with no tracked drift: `scripts/protocol-gen.ts`, `protocol-gen-swift.ts`, `protocol-gen-kotlin.ts`.
- `git diff --check` clean; docs updated (`docs/nodes/talk.md`, `docs/gateway/protocol.md`).
- Iterated under repeated adversarial autoreview (codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, xhigh) covering the confirmation-gate safety paths, transcript-loss and cross-agent-leak cases, and lifecycle races; remaining accepted tradeoffs (the informational digest is best-effort, and confirmation state is process-local like the rest of the subsystem) are documented in-code.
- The mutation digest is intentionally best-effort informational; the authoritative effects live on the call record and the canonical transcript is persisted independently.

Full CI/Testbox proof will be attached from the PR run.

target.title: fix(irc): replies produced during a disconnect window are silently dropped and falsely recorded as delivered
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where IRC agent replies produced during a transient disconnect window are silently lost. When the IRC socket drops (netsplit, server restart, or transient network blip) while an agent turn is still running, the reply handler silently no-ops on the send, and the turn is recorded as successfully delivered with a healthy outbound timestamp.

The `sendReply` closure at `extensions/irc/src/monitor.ts:171` used `client?.sendPrivmsg(target, text)` — an optional chain that silently produced nothing when `client` was set to `null` by the disconnect handler. It then unconditionally recorded `lastOutboundAt` and outbound activity, giving the operator false confidence that the reply was sent.

The existing `onError` callback at `extensions/irc/src/inbound.ts:448` already surfaces delivery errors to the runtime — it was just never reached because the send never threw. IRC has no durable retry or offline queue for this channel, so surfacing the error is the correct behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The closure now checks `if (!client) throw new Error("IRC not connected")` before the send, and `client.sendPrivmsg` is called without the optional chain (the check above guarantees client is non-null). The `statusSink` and `activity.record` calls remain after the send — they only execute on success.

When a disconnect occurs mid-turn, the reply dispatch calls `sendReply` → throws → `onError` fires → the runtime records the delivery failure and the turn is not marked delivered.

## User Impact

IRC users with unstable connections no longer see agent turns silently lost with false success indicators. The error is logged so operators can diagnose the disconnect.

## Evidence

### Source inspection (before/after)

Before (current main) — optional-chain no-op + unconditional success recording:
```ts
sendReply: async (target, text) => {
  client?.sendPrivmsg(target, text);                    // no-op when client is null
  opts.statusSink?.({ lastOutboundAt: Date.now() });    // false success
  core.channel.activity.record({ ... direction: "outbound" }); // false success
},
```

After (this patch) — explicit check + throw to surface failure:
```ts
sendReply: async (target, text) => {
  if (!client) {
    throw new Error("IRC not connected");
  }
  client.sendPrivmsg(target, text);
  opts.statusSink?.({ lastOutboundAt: Date.now() });
  core.channel.activity.record({ ... direction: "outbound" });
},
```

### Regression coverage

- Existing tests pass unchanged: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/irc/src/monitor.test.ts extensions/irc/src/send.test.ts extensions/irc/src/inbound.behavior.test.ts` → 14 passed.
- The existing reconnect test (`monitor.test.ts:168`) verifies the IRC monitor creates a new TCP connection after the first socket closes; the reconnected client's `sendPrivmsg` is a real TCP write, so send-after-reconnect is already tested.

### Sibling-surface context

The other bundled channels with real-time TCP connections (XMPP-era and equivalent) were checked: none use the same optional-chain-noop pattern with unconditional success recording. The IRC `onError` handler was the only delivery-error surface already wired but unreachable.

target.title: fix(android): stop push-to-talk from dropping speech after mid-hold pauses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android push-to-talk silently loses speech. The SpeechRecognizer PTT path runs a single recognizer session with a ~2.5 s complete-silence window, `lastTranscript` is replace-only, and the restart machinery is disabled during PTT. Consequences in a manual hold: pause mid-sentence and keep talking — everything after the recognizer's mid-hold finalization is dropped; speak two utterances — only the last final survives.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture is rebuilt as an ordered, closed rung ladder with multi-segment accumulation:

- **API 33+ raw-audio segmented** (preferred): an app-owned 16 kHz mono `AudioRecord` pumped through a `ParcelFileDescriptor` pipe into the recognizer via `EXTRA_AUDIO_SOURCE` + `EXTRA_SEGMENTED_SESSION`; `onSegmentResults` accumulates finals and the session re-arms without teardown. Input level meters from our own PCM (RMS) since `onRmsChanged` may never fire here.
- **API 33+ silence-keyed segmented**: same segment callbacks without app audio, used when raw setup fails.
- **Restart-during-hold** (below API 33 / final fallback): when a final arrives while the hold is still active, it goes into the accumulator and listening restarts — this alone fixes the dropped-speech bug on older devices.

Failed holds only descend the ladder; the speech locale (`EXTRA_LANGUAGE`) is preserved on every rung. On release, the merged transcript joins finals in order (locale-aware — no ASCII separators injected after CJK/Arabic terminal punctuation) and appends the trailing live partial unless it duplicates the last final.

The release/lifecycle semantics were the hard part and are all regression-tested: one bounded grace waits for the *terminal* recognizer callback so late finals aren't truncated (segments arriving during release accumulate without ending the wait); rapid re-press drains the prior release instead of cancelling it, so the first stop still returns its transcript; cancellation mid-release (gateway drop) tears capture down under `NonCancellable`, resumes realtime talk capture, and resolves the stop payload; callback listeners are bound to their capture id so retired sessions can't mutate the next hold; raw-rung release also calls `stopListening()` because `EXTRA_AUDIO_SOURCE` is optional and a service may legally ignore the pipe and run its own microphone.

The Live/realtime relay path is untouched — this only affects the node-invoked SpeechRecognizer PTT path.

## User Impact

Hold-to-talk stops eating speech after pauses; multi-sentence holds arrive complete; CJK/Arabic transcripts keep their punctuation; the level meter works on the raw-audio path; releases stay snappy (terminal callbacks normally arrive in well under a second — the 5 s bound only caps pathological recognizers, favoring complete transcripts over silent truncation).

## Evidence

- Focused unit tests green on Play flavor + ThirdParty compile green: `PushToTalkTranscriptMergerTest` (ordering, punctuation/no-doubling, locale punctuation, partial dedupe, empty holds), `PushToTalkRecognitionLadderTest` (descend-only selection, API gating), `TalkModeManagerTest` Robolectric regressions (segment-during-release accumulates without ending the wait; end-of-session completes it; 1.2 s late terminal final is not truncated; rapid re-press: hold A returns its transcript, hold B starts clean; cancellation mid-release clears state and next begin starts immediately).
- `:app:ktlintCheck` green; `git diff --check` clean.
- Structured autoreview: eight rounds; seven accepted findings fixed across the capture/release lifecycle (late-final truncation, raw-rung retry loop, non-terminal segment completion, re-press race, ASCII punctuation corruption, ignored-audio-source hot mic, partial cancellation teardown); final round clean — "fallback ladder, transcript accumulation, release draining, callback isolation, and audio-resource cleanup are internally consistent."
- Live device verification (real microphone/recognizer) planned before landing; not possible in the build environment.

target.title: fix(cli): bound model run image reads with per-file and aggregate budget
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `readModelRunImageFiles` function in `src/cli/capability-cli/model.ts` reads image files for model run capability. It used a TOCTOU-prone pattern: `statSync(path)` to check file size (100 MiB per-file cap + 500 MiB aggregate budget), then a separate `fs.readFile(path)` to read the content. Between the stat and the read, the file could be swapped with a much larger one, defeating the size cap.

## Why This Change Was Made

Model run files are user-supplied inputs that could be symlink-swapped or replaced between the stat validation and the read. While the per-file and aggregate budgets provide defense-in-depth, the TOCTOU window means an attacker who can control the file at the path can bypass the per-file cap. Opening the file first and operating on the same descriptor eliminates this race.

## What Changed

Replaced the path-based `statSync` + `await fs.readFile` pattern with descriptor-bound reads using `fs.promises.open`:

```typescript
const handle = await fs.open(resolvedPath, "r");
try {
  const stat = await handle.stat();
  if (!stat.isFile()) throw new Error("not a regular file");
  if (stat.size > MAX_MODEL_RUN_IMAGE_BYTES) throw new Error("file too large");
  budget.remaining -= stat.size;
  return await handle.readFile();
} finally {
  await handle.close();
}
```

Key points:
- `fs.promises.open()` returns a `FileHandle` — `stat()` and `readFile()` both operate on the same descriptor
- `try/finally` guarantees `handle.close()` even when exceptions are thrown
- Per-file 100 MiB cap and 500 MiB aggregate budget are preserved from the original implementation
- `import { statSync }` was removed as no longer needed
- Sequential processing (already in original) is retained

## User Impact

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| `statSync(path)` → TOCTOU race: file could be swapped before read | → fd pins the inode; race impossible |
| Normal model run with valid files → works | → works (unchanged) |
| Per-file 100 MiB cap + 500 MiB aggregate budget | → preserved, now without TOCTOU |

## Evidence

**All 109 capability-cli tests pass:**

```
 ✓ |cli| src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts (109 tests) 3133ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  109 passed (109)
```

The descriptor-bound pattern is the standard fix for TOCTOU file races — the fd pins the specific inode, preventing substitution between validation and consumption.

## Real Behavior Proof

Ran the production `openclaw --dev capability model run --local` command against real image files using the branch build. Paths redacted to `<tmp>`.

### Accepted image (within 100 MiB per-file cap)

```
$ openclaw --dev capability model run --prompt "hello" --file <tmp>/tiny.png --local --json
```

Relevant JSON excerpt:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "capability": "model.run",
  "transport": "local",
  "inputs": [
    {
      "path": "<tmp>/tiny.png",
      "mimeType": "image/png"
    }
  ],
  "outputs": [
    {
      "text": "Hello! I see that you've mentioned an image...",
      "mediaUrl": null
    }
  ]
}
```

The 70-byte PNG is accepted, loaded via the descriptor-bound path, and passed to the model as an `image/png` input.

### Per-file rejection (>100 MiB)

```
$ openclaw --dev capability model run --prompt "hello" --file <tmp>/huge.png --local --json
```

Output:

```
Error: --file too large: <tmp>/huge.png is 110100480 bytes (max 104857600)
```

The 105 MiB file is rejected before any read, because the size check is performed on the same opened file descriptor that would be used for `readFile`.

### Aggregate-budget rejection (>500 MiB total)

```
$ openclaw --dev capability model run --prompt "hello" \
  --file <tmp>/medium1.png --file <tmp>/medium2.png --file <tmp>/medium3.png \
  --file <tmp>/medium4.png --file <tmp>/medium5.png --file <tmp>/medium6.png \
  --local --json
```

Output:

```
Error: --file too large: <tmp>/medium6.png is 94371840 bytes (max remaining total budget 52428800)
```

Six 90 MiB images total 540 MiB. The first five consume 450 MiB of the 500 MiB aggregate budget; the sixth is rejected because it exceeds the remaining 50 MiB, proving the aggregate cap is enforced across the invocation.

target.title: fix(openai): reject malformed Codex image base64
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users generating images through the OpenAI Codex Responses route could receive a truncated or corrupted image when the SSE response contained malformed Base64 image data. Node's permissive decoder silently discarded invalid characters instead of surfacing the bad provider response.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Codex image decoder now trims the payload the same way Codex does, then validates and canonicalizes it with the existing media-runtime helper before decoding. The existing encoded-size limit is preserved and other OpenAI image routes are unchanged. The compatibility risk is limited to malformed Codex image results: inputs accepted by Codex's strict decoder remain accepted, including surrounding Unicode whitespace.

## User Impact

Malformed Codex image responses now fail with a clear provider-owned error instead of returning corrupted image bytes. Valid image responses continue to work normally.

## Evidence

Current dependency contract check: Codex `origin/main` at [`0fb559f`](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/0fb559f0f6e231a88ac02ea002d3ecd248e2b515) models the image payload as the `result` string of an `image_generation_call` ([protocol model](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/0fb559f0f6e231a88ac02ea002d3ecd248e2b515/codex-rs/protocol/src/models.rs#L987-L1006)). Before saving, Codex applies `result.trim()` and decodes with `BASE64_STANDARD` ([decoder](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/0fb559f0f6e231a88ac02ea002d3ecd248e2b515/codex-rs/ext/image-generation/src/tool.rs#L230-L239)). Its workspace pins `base64` 0.22.1 ([dependency](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/0fb559f0f6e231a88ac02ea002d3ecd248e2b515/codex-rs/Cargo.toml#L282)); that crate's `STANDARD` engine requires the standard alphabet, canonical padding, and valid trailing bits ([configuration](https://github.com/marshallpierce/rust-base64/blob/v0.22.1/src/engine/general_purpose/mod.rs#L251-L263), [STANDARD engine](https://github.com/marshallpierce/rust-base64/blob/v0.22.1/src/engine/general_purpose/mod.rs#L331-L347)).

The proposed decoder now mirrors Codex's surrounding Unicode trim before calling OpenClaw's existing Base64 validator. That validator accepts the standard alphabet and canonical padding and is additionally tolerant of missing padding and ASCII whitespace, so this path is not stricter than Codex for valid standard-Base64 results. A committed positive regression test covers Codex-compatible surrounding Unicode whitespace, alongside malformed-payload tests for both terminal SSE event shapes.

Before/after behavior was exercised with a temporary local proof test that started a real `node:http` TCP server on `127.0.0.1`, returned Codex Responses SSE events, and called `buildOpenAIImageGenerationProvider().generateImage(...)` with the configured private-network opt-in. Only auth resolution used a fixed `test-token`; the production provider, SSRF handling, HTTP request, bounded SSE reader/parser, decoder, and result construction were used unchanged.

On current `upstream/main`, the malformed payload `aGVs!bG8=` was accepted and silently decoded to the five bytes for `hello`, so the negative assertion failed as expected:

```text
FAIL ... rejects malformed image data through real HTTP and SSE
AssertionError: promise resolved ... instead of rejecting
buffer data: [104, 101, 108, 108, 111]
Tests 1 failed | 1 skipped
```

With this change, the same real HTTP/SSE proof rejected the malformed payload while its valid Base64 control decoded to `hello`:

```text
✓ rejects malformed image data through real HTTP and SSE 241ms
✓ accepts valid image data through real HTTP and SSE 5ms
Test Files 1 passed (1)
Tests 2 passed (2)
```

Focused regression suite before the follow-up compatibility test:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.test.ts
Test Files 1 passed (1)
Tests 71 passed (71)
```

Additional checks: targeted `oxfmt`, targeted `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed. `autoreview --mode uncommitted` reported no accepted/actionable findings (`patch is correct`, confidence `0.96`). The follow-up commit passed `git diff --check`; full validation, including its committed Unicode-whitespace regression, is running in GitHub Actions. Live OpenAI credentials were not available, so no request was sent to the hosted provider.

AI-assisted: Codex helped implement and review this change; the source inspection and all evidence above were run manually.

target.title: fix(oc-path): bound config file reads with size cap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two unbounded file reads in `extensions/oc-path/src/cli.ts`:

1. `loadAst` (line 164): reads the entire config file into memory to parse as JSONC/JSONL/YAML/Markdown AST, with no size limit
2. `set` command diff read (line 335): reads the "old" file content for `--diff` output, with no size limit

Both paths use user-supplied CLI arguments (`openclaw path resolve <file>`, `openclaw path set <file>`) — a user could accidentally point to a large file and OOM the CLI.

## Why This Change Was Made

Unbounded `fs.readFile` on user-controlled paths is a valid OOM vector. While oc-path files are typically small config files, there is no defense against multi-GB input.

## What Changed

Added `loadOcPathFileSafely` helper that:
1. Stats the file via `statSync`
2. Rejects non-regular files
3. Rejects files exceeding 10 MiB
4. Only reads files that pass the checks

Applied to both the `loadAst` path and the `set --diff` path.

## User Impact

| `openclaw path resolve ./10GB-config.json` → OOM | → rejected with "file too large" |

| Normal small config files → works | → works (unchanged) |

target.title: fix(openshell): bound sandbox readFile with size cap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `readFile` method in `extensions/openshell/src/fs-bridge.ts` (line 72) opens a file through the sandbox bridge and calls `handle.readFile()` to read the entire file as a Buffer with no size limit. A sandboxed process could request reading a multi-GB file, causing OOM in the host process.

While the sandbox already validates path safety (symlinks, hardlinks), it imposes no size limit on file reads.

## Why This Change Was Made

Unbounded file reads in the sandbox bridge is a real OOM vector. A sandboxed agent process can request arbitrary file reads through the `SandboxFsBridge` interface, and without a size cap, a large file (or a compromised sandbox process) could exhaust host memory.

## What Changed

Added a `handle.stat()` check before `readFile()` in `OpenShellFsBridge.readFile`:
1. Stats the opened file handle
2. Rejects non-regular files
3. Rejects files exceeding 100 MiB cap
4. Only proceeds to `readFile()` for files that pass the checks

## User Impact

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| Sandbox read of 10 GB file → host OOM | → rejected with "file too large" |
| Normal sandbox file reads → works | → works (unchanged) |

target.title: chore(docker): bundle channel voice plugin deps
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: default Docker builds pruned optional bundled plugin runtime dependencies unless operators knew to set `OPENCLAW_EXTENSIONS`.
- Why it matters: Discord, Feishu, and Voice Call are externalized plugin packages but should be ready in the standard Docker image path.
- What changed: default Docker image builds now include bundled plugin ids `discord`, `feishu`, and `voice-call`; `scripts/docker/setup.sh` uses the same default.
- What did NOT change: operators can still pass `OPENCLAW_EXTENSIONS=` to build a slimmer image without optional bundled plugin deps.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Docs
- [x] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Integrations
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: default Docker setup/image-build inputs now include the bundled plugin ids `discord feishu voice-call`, while an explicitly empty `OPENCLAW_EXTENSIONS=` remains an opt-out.
- Real environment tested: Linux repo checkout, Node 22.22.0, Docker setup-script command path exercised through the repository Docker setup harness; full container image build is left to the PR image-build check.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `corepack pnpm test src/dockerfile.test.ts src/docker-setup.e2e.test.ts` and `corepack pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 Dockerfile scripts/docker/setup.sh docs/install/docker.md src/dockerfile.test.ts src/docker-setup.e2e.test.ts CHANGELOG.md`.
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output): copied terminal output:

```text
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.unit-fast.config.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  14 passed (14)

[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  28 passed (28)

[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 12.88s

Checking formatting...
All matched files use the correct format.
Finished in 5469ms on 4 files using 1 threads.
```

- Observed result after fix: the Docker setup harness output included `--build-arg OPENCLAW_EXTENSIONS=discord feishu voice-call` for default setup and preserved `--build-arg OPENCLAW_EXTENSIONS=` for the explicit empty opt-out path.
- What was not tested: full Docker image build locally; I am monitoring PR CI for image-build proof.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): before this patch, `Dockerfile` defaulted `ARG OPENCLAW_EXTENSIONS=""`, and `scripts/docker/setup.sh` exported an empty `OPENCLAW_EXTENSIONS` default.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Default Docker image builds include Discord, Feishu, and Voice Call plugin runtime dependencies. Custom slim builds can opt out with `OPENCLAW_EXTENSIONS=`.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A

## Repro + Verification

```text
corepack pnpm docs:list
corepack pnpm test src/dockerfile.test.ts src/docker-setup.e2e.test.ts
corepack pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 Dockerfile scripts/docker/setup.sh docs/install/docker.md src/dockerfile.test.ts src/docker-setup.e2e.test.ts CHANGELOG.md
git diff --check
```

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Dockerfile default, setup-script default, explicit empty `OPENCLAW_EXTENSIONS` opt-out, Docker docs formatting.
- Edge cases checked: explicit empty env var does not fall back to defaults.
- What you did not verify: full Docker image build locally; this PR relies on the image-build CI for that proof.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Config/env changes? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Migration needed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: none; set `OPENCLAW_EXTENSIONS=` to keep the previous slim optional-plugin behavior.

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: default Docker images include more plugin dependencies.
  - Mitigation: document and test `OPENCLAW_EXTENSIONS=` as an opt-out.

target.title: fix: catch body cancel rejections in redirect and proxy-validation paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Same pattern as today's PRs #111106 (tlon), #111105 (matrix), and #111081 (tlon): `void response.body?.cancel()` can produce an unhandled promise rejection when the ReadableStream underlying source cancel throws. Two sites in core infra code had this pattern.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `.catch(() => undefined)` so body cancellation failures in redirect processing (fetch-guard.ts) and proxy validation probes (proxy-validation.ts) cannot produce unhandled rejections.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change — body cancel is always best-effort cleanup. Prevents potential Node.js process warnings from unhandled rejections during HTTP redirect following and proxy validation.

## Evidence

- Added a focused test in `src/infra/net/fetch-guard.ssrf.test.ts` that drives `fetchWithSsrFGuard` through a 302 → 200 redirect where the redirect response body has a rejecting `cancel()`. Asserts the final 200 response is returned and no `unhandledRejection` occurs.
- Added a focused test in `src/infra/net/proxy/proxy-validation.test.ts` that mocks the proxy agent/dispatcher and drives the default fetch probe with a response whose body `cancel()` rejects. Asserts the validation result is preserved and no `unhandledRejection` occurs.

target.title: fix(msteams): catch body cancel rejections in attachment fetch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The same pattern fixed in today's PRs #111106 (tlon), #111105 (matrix), and #111081 (tlon): `response.body?.cancel()` can reject when the ReadableStream underlying source cancel method throws, which produces an unhandled promise rejection. The MS Teams attachment fetch code had 7 unprotected cancel() calls across two files, while bot-framework.ts already had the .catch() fix at one call site (line 211) — suggesting the others were simply overlooked.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `.catch(() => undefined)` to all remaining `response.body?.cancel()` calls in the MS Teams attachment fetch path so body cancellation failures cannot produce unhandled rejections.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change — the body cancel is always a best-effort cleanup. This prevents potential Node.js process warnings or crash paths from unhandled rejections during attachment download retries.

## Evidence

- Added shared helper `extensions/msteams/src/attachments/test-helpers.ts` that builds a `Response` whose `ReadableStream.cancel()` rejects.
- Added focused regression coverage in `extensions/msteams/src/attachments/bot-framework.test.ts` for the four changed cancel sites:
  - `attachmentInfo` non-OK response
  - `attachmentView` non-OK response
  - `attachmentView` invalid `content-length`
  - `attachmentView` `content-length` > `maxBytes`
- Added `extensions/msteams/src/attachments/download.test.ts` covering the three changed cancel sites in `fetchWithAuthFallback`:
  - first attempt 401 → cancel before auth fallback
  - auth attempt non-401/403 → cancel and continue to next scope
  - auth attempt 401/403 → cancel before next scope
- All new tests assert the function returns the expected result and `unhandledRejection` is empty.

target.title: fix(ci): skip Periphery scans for unrelated PR changes
target.body:
Related: #106090
Observed on: #106789

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where pull requests unrelated to iOS, macOS, or shared OpenClawKit could run Periphery scans when `main` advanced after the pull-request event was created. The stale event base SHA made base-branch changes look like pull-request changes, consuming macOS runners and adding irrelevant checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The three Periphery scope jobs now compare GitHub's synthetic pull-request merge commit with its first parent, which is the exact base tree used to build that merge result. Checkout depth is increased to two so both commits are available; the stale event-base fetch is no longer needed.

Scope behavior remains fail-closed, manual dispatch still scans, draft pull requests still skip, and renamed files remain covered.

## User Impact

Unrelated pull requests no longer start iOS, macOS, or shared OpenClawKit Periphery scan jobs solely because `main` changed. Pull requests that actually touch the scoped native paths continue to run the same scans.

AI-assisted change; I reviewed and understand the implementation and tests.

## Evidence

- Regression test builds a hermetic synthetic merge where `main` adds a shared OpenClawKit file while the PR changes only docs. The old event-base comparison reports a scoped change; `HEAD^1..HEAD` reports only the PR's docs file and sets `should-scan=false`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/periphery-scope-workflows.test.ts test/scripts/ios-periphery-comment-workflow.test.ts test/scripts/periphery-intersection.test.ts` — 3 files, 36 tests passed.
- `node scripts/check-workflows.mjs` — passed, including zizmor and interpolation checks.
- `oxfmt --check` on all six touched files — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Fresh autoreview — no accepted/actionable findings; patch correct at 0.96 confidence.
- Blacksmith Testbox run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29387812718 reached ready state but the delegated host DNS timed out before repository commands could execute. target.title: fix(web): apply Control UI text size to content typography
target.body:
## Summary

In this PR, the Appearance text-size setting applies across Control UI content typography instead of only affecting the chat transcript. Shared content font sizes now route through `--control-ui-text-scale`, while touch-primary text-entry controls keep the existing 16px minimum so the 90% text-size stop does not reintroduce mobile Safari focus zoom.

## Screenshots

Settings at the default M text size, showing the Appearance text-size control in English.

![Settings text size at M](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-settings-text-size-m-en.png)

Overview at XXL text size, showing the larger page typography across cards and form controls.

![Overview using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-overview-xxl-en.png)

Channels at XXL text size, showing the larger channel cards and actions.

![Channels using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-channels-xxl-en.png)

Mobile Overview at XXL text size, showing the narrow layout with scaled content typography.

![Mobile overview using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-mobile-overview-xxl-en.png)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Appearance text-size setting so it affects Control UI content typography beyond the chat transcript. Before this PR, the setting could be saved while many Settings, quick settings, overview, channel, session, skill, and content surfaces still used fixed font sizes.

## Why This Change Was Made

In this PR, shared Control UI font sizes route through the existing `--control-ui-text-scale` value instead of hard-coded pixel sizes. The change keeps layout chrome and spacing stable while letting readable content, forms, cards, chat text, composer text, and page typography respond to S/M/L/XL/XXL.

Touch-primary text-entry controls keep the existing `--control-ui-input-text-size` minimum so the 90% text-size stop does not shrink mobile inputs below 16px and reintroduce Safari focus zoom.

## User Impact

Changing Text size in Appearance now produces visible typography changes across the main product surfaces, while M remains the normal/default size.

## Validation

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

The Control UI mock has limited curated chat state for design QA, so reviewers have to rely on ad hoc sessions when checking empty chat, longer transcripts, markdown rendering, code blocks, tables, warnings, and recoverable error copy.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR adds stable dev/mock-only fixture sessions to the Control UI mock server. The proposed fixtures cover a New session empty state, a coding session, a response-shape showcase, and a markdown showcase without changing production gateway or session APIs.

## User Impact

There is no production user-facing behavior change. Developers and designers can load stable mock chat sessions for future Control UI visual review.

target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```text

    ],
    "exclude": [
      "vision_map.click_at",

```

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs
codex review --base origin/main
```

Regression coverage added: `src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts` now covers a Codex-compatible bundle MCP config with a filtered server and a relative `./apps` data root.

Validation results:

```text

pnpm check:docs: Docs formatting clean; markdownlint 0 errors; MDX check passed; i18n glossary passed; checked_internal_links=4554; broken_links=0
codex review --base origin/main: No actionable correctness issues were found
```

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime change. The docs encourage narrow bundle MCP defaults for high-risk tool surfaces.

What is the highest-risk area? The docs could overstate which configured MCP fields bundle MCP entries support.

How is that risk mitigated? Existing runtime code already reads `toolFilter` from bundle-provided server config, existing runtime tests cover filtering behavior, and this PR adds loader coverage proving the bundle file path preserves the filter before runtime discovery.

AI-assisted: yes.

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```
openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```
node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs   # imports FIELD_HELP and buildPromptSection from this branch
```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):

```
$ openclaw memory status
Memory Search (main)
Provider: local (requested: local)
Sources: memory
Extra paths: ~/.openclaw/shared-memory
Indexed: 105/105 files . 933 chunks
Workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku
By source:
  memory . 105/105 files . 933 chunks
```

```
$ openclaw memory index
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
Memory index updated (main).
```

```
$ openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
0.812 memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md:1-9
    Recursive memory search proof.
    Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
    This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
    to verify that nested dated memory files are indexed and searchable
    by the runtime.

0.450 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md:1-6
0.432 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/pr-draft.md:1-32
```

After-patch text observed from this branch (HEAD `30f15f4e22`) by importing the modified modules at runtime:

```
$ node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs
=== schema.help.ts: FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch'] ===
Vector search over MEMORY.md and memory/**/*.md (per-agent overrides supported).

=== prompt-section.ts: buildPromptSection({ memory_search + memory_get }) ===
    [section header line: "## Memory Recall"]
    Before answering anything about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos: run memory_search on MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md + indexed session transcripts; then use memory_get to pull only the needed lines. If low confidence after search, say you checked.
    Citations are disabled: do not mention file paths or line numbers in replies unless the user explicitly asks.

=== prompt-section.ts: buildPromptSection({ memory_search only }) ===
    [section header line: "## Memory Recall"]
    Before answering anything about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos: run memory_search on MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md + indexed session transcripts and answer from the matching results. If low confidence after search, say you checked.
    Citations are disabled: do not mention file paths or line numbers in replies unless the user explicitly asks.

=== extensions/memory-core/index.ts (post-patch source lines) ===
 127      description:
 128        "Mandatory recall step: semantically search MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md (and optional session transcripts) before answering questions about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos. ...",

 139      description:
 140        "Safe exact excerpt read from MEMORY.md or memory/**/*.md. Defaults to a bounded excerpt when lines are omitted, includes truncation/continuation info when more content exists, and `corpus=wiki` reads from registered compiled-wiki supplements.",

=== extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts (post-patch source lines) ===
 240      description:
 241        "Mandatory recall step: semantically search MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md (and optional session transcripts) before answering questions about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos. ...",

 410      description:
 411        "Safe exact excerpt read from MEMORY.md or memory/**/*.md. Defaults to a bounded excerpt when lines are omitted, includes truncation/continuation info when more content exists, and `corpus=wiki` reads from registered compiled-wiki supplements.",
```

**Observed result after fix**: (a) The freshly written nested file `memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md` (two levels deep under `memory/`) was indexed by `openclaw memory index` and returned as the top match (score `0.812`) for the unique token. A second nested hit from `memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md` (three levels deep) confirms recursion is not limited to one level. (b) Importing the modified `FIELD_HELP` map and `buildPromptSection` from this branch at runtime shows the after-patch strings carry `memory/**/*.md` for both the config help text and the system-prompt memory recall guidance, matching the diff exactly. (c) The two `memory_search` / `memory_get` description strings in `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` and `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` are inline string literals; the after-patch lines printed from this branch show the new wording in place. No runtime code paths are modified, only the descriptor and doc strings plus the regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`.

**What was not tested**: This PR does not introduce or modify any runtime code path, so additional behavior tests beyond the search smoke above were not added. The recursive walk itself (`collectMemoryFilesFromDir`) is already covered by upstream tests under `packages/memory-host-sdk/`.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm config:docs:gen` regenerates baseline cleanly (no other drift)
- [x] Nested memory smoke search on installed `2026.5.20` returns the new nested file at score `0.812`
- [x] On-branch runtime import shows `FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch']`, `buildPromptSection(...)` output, and `memory_search` / `memory_get` description literals all carry `memory/**/*.md`
- [ ] CI: lint / type / config-baseline check
